title: Epochal KV offset mismatch - reproduction breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent mismatch between KV cache offsets and attention window observed when sequence lengths cross epoch boundaries (long prompt + continued session). Symptoms: stale tokens served from KV layer, attention reading a previous epoch's keys, leading to hallucinated repetition or truncated context. Repro is flaky but correlates with: long prefixes (~>12k tokens), repeated incremental generation (streaming on), and kernel fallback to "small-ctx" attention path during a burst.

Observed incidents (brief):
- 2025-10-29 04:17 UTC: customer A reported truncated context for multi-turn assistant; trace shows tokens 0..10240 were present but attention acted like last 2048 only.
- 2025-11-01 12:03 UTC: local stress run (see steps below) produced mismatched KVOFFSET marker in kv-index at epoch boundary; session ID 6a7f3e.

Hypothesis summary (working):
1) When sequence length grows past a compiled kernel's optimized threshold, runtime switches attention kernel mid-request (or mid-session) causing KV index mapping to use a different offset base (epoch), leading to reads at wrong absolute positions.
2) There is a race between KV prefetch eviction and prefix-rotation code: eviction marks slot N free while concurrent attention lookup still expects N -> yields ghost reads.
3) Quantized model variants (q4_* paths) use a different KV slot layout padding which is not fully reconciled by the kernel-selection shim.

Repro steps (deterministic experiment I run locally):
1) Start local serving runtime with debug kv logging enabled:
   export RW_DEBUG_KV=1 RW_DEBUG_ATTEN=1 RW_MAX_SEQ=16384
   ./bin/serve --model rwd-open-7b --listen 127.0.0.1:5100 --kernels=cpu,small-ctx,large-ctx --quantize=auto
2) Create a client that does incremental streaming generation with an initial prefix of ~10k tokens, then append generated tokens until total ~13k. Use deterministic sampling (temp=0.0) to reduce nondeterminism.
3) Capture logs: /tmp/kvtrace-<session>.log and runtime debug output. Also capture memory maps (nvidia-smi top at the time).

Commands I ran (paste):
- start server (local):
  RW_DEBUG_KV=1 RW_DEBUG_ATTEN=1 RW_MAX_SEQ=16384 ./bin/serve --model rwd-open-7b --listen 127.0.0.1:5100 --kernels=large-ctx,small-ctx --quantize=auto 2>&1 | tee /tmp/serve-epochal.log

- reproduce client (python snippet):
  python experiments/stream_repro.py --host 127.0.0.1:5100 --prefix-file experiments/long_prefix_10k.txt --generate 3000 --deterministic true --session-id repro-epochal

- tail KV traces:
  grep KVOFF /tmp/serve-epochal.log | tail -n 200 > /tmp/kv-kvoff-tail.log

Example log dump (sanitized):
[2025-11-01T12:02:48.912Z] KVCACHE: session=repro-epochal alloc slot=123 epoch=42 base_offset=4096 KVOFF=4096
[2025-11-01T12:02:49.014Z] ATTEN: select_kernel -> large-ctx (seq=10240)
[2025-11-01T12:02:49.798Z] ATTEN: fallback_kernel -> small-ctx (seq=11264) // fallback due to mem pressure
[2025-11-01T12:02:49.799Z] KVCACHE: lookup session=repro-epochal slot=123 read_offset=4096 epoch=41 -> returned tokens range 0..2048 (MISMATCH)
[2025-11-01T12:02:49.799Z] WARNING: kv-read-epoch != expected; expected=42 got=41

Stack-ish trace (coarse):
- client -> serving runtime recv->route -> request handled by worker-7 -> attention dispatch picks kernel 'large-ctx' -> before kernel finishes, memory pressure triggers background eviction -> eviction code rotate_epoch(session, new_epoch=42) -> kernel falls back to 'small-ctx' mid-eval -> small-ctx uses older slot indices that weren't updated -> mismatch observed.

Commands tried to probe kernel switching behavior:
- toggled kernel ordering: --kernels=large-ctx,small-ctx vs small-ctx,large-ctx -> affects frequency but doesn't eliminate.
- disabled autoshrink: --kv-disable-evict -> reduced incidence but still reproducible under heavy CPU pressure.
- forced no-fallback: set RW_KERNEL_FALLBACK=0 -> reproduction failed (good sign) but not viable in prod.

Test matrix notes (what I ran and results):
- Model variant q4_0 vs q8_0: q4 shows 3x higher mismatch rate. Hypothesis: padding/layout differences.
- Sequence lengths tested: 8k, 10k, 12k, 14k. Spike around crossing 11-12k where kernel chooses fallback.
- Streams on vs off: streaming (incremental kv writes) increases repro probability.

Small experiments / artifacts:
- quick diff of kv-index before/after rotation:
  $ ./bin/kvtool dump-index --session repro-epochal --out /tmp/idx-before.json
  (generate ~1k tokens)
  $ ./bin/kvtool dump-index --session repro-epochal --out /tmp/idx-after.json
  diff -u /tmp/idx-before.json /tmp/idx-after.json | head -n 80
  -> saw slot 123 had epoch: 41 -> 42 and base_offset changed but lookup code read using stale epoch variable in worker thread.

Error snippets I captured (raw):
- "WARNING kv-read-epoch != expected; expected=42 got=41"
- "ATTN_FALLBACK: kernel_switch mid-exec (worker-7) reason=OOM_PRESSURE"
- "KVCACHE: ghost-read slot=123 session=repro-epochal"

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is there a memory barrier missing when we write new epoch metadata to shared KV index? Looks like a missing atomic publish.
- Does the kernel-selection shim update thread-local kernel metadata before the kernel starts, or can mid-run kernel switches leave stale thread-local epoch pointers?
- Are there race windows introduced by background prefetch + eviction + kernel fallback that we didn't account for?

Quick code pointers to inspect next:
- runtime/kv/cache_manager.cc -> rotate_epoch() (possible missing memory_fence/publish)
- runtime/attn/kernel_shim.cc -> switch_kernel() (verify worker thread state ordering)
- runtime/quant/kv_layout.h -> layout differences across quant bits

Immediate next steps (ordered):
1) Add an assert in kv lookup: assert(read_epoch == expected_epoch || log full context) to catch first occurrence in prod-like runs. (low-risk)
2) Instrument kernel_shim to emit kernel-switch boundaries and worker-local epoch snapshot. (medium)
3) Reproduce with --disable-evict + artificially toggle kernels via script to isolate race (high-confidence repro if race exists).
4) Run long_prefix + forced mid-kernel kernel-switch test using fault-injection: simulate fallback by sending SIGUSR1 to worker to trigger forced switch.
5) If confirmed, fix order in rotate_epoch(): publish index update, memory_fence, then flip session->epoch pointer with atomic store.

Notes to self (timeline / breadcrumbs):
- 2025-11-04: Added extra log lines, repro rate jumped 7% (we exposed more failures).
- 2025-11-09: Claire ran dynmem stress and saw same sign on real hardware.
- 2025-11-20: Ben tried test with RW_KERNEL_FALLBACK=0 ; no repro. Suggests kernel fallback is causal, not just correlated.

Slack threads / links to poke before next meeting:
- #eng-serving-runtime: thread "kv epoch mismatch" (pinned messages)
- PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/1423 (instrumentation WIP)

Possible mitigations for customer-facing incidents (short-term):
- Temporary: Set RW_KERNEL_FALLBACK=0 for affected clusters (reduces stability but avoids corruption).
- Medium: Force eviction to block kernel-switch (coarse lock) while we patch ordering.
- Long: Fix ordering and add aggressive fuzz tests around kernel-switch + kv-rotation.

Unresolved and TODO (brief):
- [ ] Confirm atomic publish semantics in rotate_epoch() using valgrind/helgrind on linux worker image (Ben)
- [ ] Add kernel-switch epoch snapshot instrumentation and run CI fuzz for 48 hours (Ravi)
- [ ] Add unit test that simulates layout differences between quantized and full-precision variants (Claire)

Random heuristics I want to try (notes):
- Insert small epoch-padding window: bump base_offset by 16 slots on rotate to prevent immediate reuse -> might mask but show whether reuse is root cause.
- Make kernel_shim do an explicit publish/handshake with worker before allowing fallback to complete.

If you pick this up: start with reproducer script (experiments/stream_repro.py) and iterate on the logs. Keep session id repro-epochal. If you add logs, try to keep records small (zip /tmp/kvtrace-*.log).

End of scratchpad.

(Notes intentionally messy — this is a working breadcrumbs file; follow up via Slack or push to PR for instrumentation.)
